judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Assigned by a foreman to include among other duties the operation of a hi-lo fork lift truck (not including any type walk truck)' is definite, with the exclusion spelled out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallel in form to the 2-E.2(j) tractor-trailer bonus; no conflicting provision found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Straightforward: seniority lists by length of service, used to order layoffs; the inclusion of foremen on the lists is the only oddity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 6-B lets the Publisher appoint and remove foremen freely and set their terms individually, which sits awkwardly with placing foremen on the contractual seniority list.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Otherwise seniority is herein defined as length of service based on regularity and continuity of service' is a circular definition, and 'otherwise' is unexplained.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read against 4-A.1(a)'s different, service-with-the-newspaper measure for regular situation holders, producing two seniority concepts in one subsection.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definitional lead-in; nothing to construe on its own.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Depends on 4-A.1's list of regular situation holders; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Group 1 definition ends with 'or for other such good and sufficient cause' after enumerated causes — an ejusdem generis catch-all — and 'shape steadily' is vague.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Industry' is defined in 4-A.2(i) and the groups drive 13-A wage tiers and 13-H contribution tiers, so group classification has consequences elsewhere but no contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A two-item promotion order; concise and clear, though it omits Groups 2 and 4 without saying so.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 4-B says vacancies are filled permanently from among regular situation holders by seniority yet 'in accord with 4-A.2(c)' on a temporary basis; reconciling the two orders of preference is genuinely awkward.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single sentence tying hiring order to the Board's most recent lists; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 4-A.2(g) and 4-G on list maintenance and posting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed shape rules, but 'except where competency is a factor' is an undefined escape from the failure-to-shape rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cross-refers to the 4-F exceptions and vacation/holiday credit, which fit together; the Adjustment Board under 16-H has exclusive jurisdiction over such disputes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence tie-break rule with no standard given, but nothing ambiguous in its operation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 16-H giving the Adjustment Board exclusive jurisdiction over Section 4-A.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The proviso allowing a foreman to 'engage such men as he may be able to obtain' when the list runs short is a broad exception to exclusive Board control stated in the same paragraph.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That exception echoes the closed-shop text quarantined in 17-A.1 and sits against 2-L.2's membership requirement, raising a coherence question.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear prohibition with a dated grandfather exception.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Complements 4-A.3 (no regular situation in more than one shop); no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defines 'industry' by an enumerated list of company types plus a geographic limit; the list's completeness (e.g., printing plants, distributors of other publications) is arguable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The definition feeds Group 1 and 2 listings in 4-A.2(b), 7-A's 'elsewhere in the industry', and 4-F leaves 'from the industry', so a narrow or broad reading has knock-on effects.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An introductory sentence subject to limitations that follow; nothing ambiguous alone.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Works with (j)(1)–(3) and 4-A.2(b) Group 1; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise five-year continuous-holding requirement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Group 1 listing scheme; nothing conflicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise percentage cap tied to a fixed measuring date.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits with (j)(3)'s allocation of that same 2% between signatory and non-signatory sources.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The one-third and two-thirds fractions are OCR-garbled but the structure is clear; the two limbs total the whole 2% allowance.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Depends on and is consistent with (j)(2); no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line prohibition; unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 4-A.2(h) and Group 1's exclusion of those holding situations elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Qualified and competent for the work or the job in question' is an open-textured standard, though a common one.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 4-H routes competency questions to the Board and 2-I limits refusal of employment on competency grounds, which fit together.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conditional conformity clause with clear scope limits ('with respect to the parties against whom such order shall run').
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallel to 17-B's general separability clause; both are consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Internally tangled: filled 'immediately' on a temporary basis, yet posted for four weeks and 'filled immediately at the end of that four week period', and 'not in excess of five' subsequent vacancies is unexplained.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It uses 4-A.2(c)'s promotion order for the temporary fill but seniority among regular situation holders for the permanent fill, and 2-E.2(b) cross-refers here for driver selection.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear consequences for refusal, though placing an unemployed extra 'at the top' and a regular extra 'at the end' of the same list is a striking asymmetry that could be read as an error.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the group hierarchy in 4-A.2(b)–(c); nothing contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Grammatically defective ('If a regular situation holder or an extra accept ... and then be found to be unqualified'), and 'the first vacancy ... which occurs in the course of filling the situation just vacated by him' is hard to apply.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Interacts with 4-B's chain of subsequent vacancies and 4-A.4's competence rule; workable but intricate.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear reverse-seniority layoff rule with a two-week notice requirement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be squared with 3-D.1's economic layoff right, 3-D.5's excess-situation mechanism and 20-E.6's waiver of layoff rights, but each is expressly reconciled.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Partial incapacitation by reason of advanced age' and 'a leave of absence from the industry' are vague, and the enumerated exceptions leave the residual scope uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its exceptions are incorporated by 4-A.2(e) for shape credit and it operates alongside 4-F.2 restoration; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Shall not be unreasonably withheld' is a standard but genuinely open reasonableness test, used twice.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Ties into 4-F.1(a)(4)'s exception for leaves of absence; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Unless an explanation for the absence is received' sets no standard for what explanation suffices.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It qualifies 4-F.1(a)'s automatic vacatur, and the two read together leave unclear whether an explanation alone preserves the situation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short restoration rule; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Follows directly from 4-F.1(a)'s list of protected absences; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A posting and furnishing obligation; plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 4-A.2(g) and 3-A.3 posting requirements.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A broad but conventional referral clause ('any question ... or otherwise with respect to the interpretation or application of these provisions').
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 16-H gives the Adjustment Board 'exclusive jurisdiction' over Section 4-A issues, while this clause routes them to the Joint Standing Committee/Appeals Board — a genuine allocation conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: '7 hours and 54 minutes or less consecutively between the period of 7:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m.' is precise, if oddly specific.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5-B's night shift runs from 6:00 p.m. to 10:00 a.m., overlapping the day shift window of 7:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m., so shift classification for overlapping hours is genuinely uncertain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Short nights' and 'one long night' are used without definition here, and the Saturday period beginning at 4:00 p.m. conflicts with the stated 6:00 p.m.–10:00 a.m. window.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5-D fixes the weekly night pattern and lets the Publisher pick the long night, and 5-A's day-shift window overlaps this one.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The weekly hour figure is garbled ('8915 hours') so the numerical limit cannot be read off the text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5-A's daily 7h54m over five days would give 39.5 hours, which suggests the intended figure and is consistent; 5-F keys overtime to these limits.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The stated 36.5-hour week does not add up to the itemised nights (3x7 + 8 + 7.5 = 36.5 only if all five are worked), and the figures are OCR-garbled.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5-B defines the same shifts and 5-F keys overtime to 'the five-day or five-night period'; the arithmetic ties out, so no true conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short pay guarantee tied to defined shifts; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 13-A rate tables and 5-A/5-B definitions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A layered definition with three alternative triggers, the last ('before or after the hour at which the shift ... begins or terminates') potentially overlapping the first.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 13-D fixes the overtime rate and 5-M requires overtime to be worked; 7-B provides a different holiday-overtime rate, which is an express carve-out rather than a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'So that as many regular situations as possible may be created and maintained' is an aspirational standard with no measurable content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 3-D.6 expressly subordinates this duty to 3-D.1's layoff right and Section 16, which is an acknowledged tension between the two.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The trigger — an evening paper 'of which the full printing and circulation does not begin until after 12:01 a.m., Sunday' — is convoluted but determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5-K pays only time and one-half for Sunday work in the 10 a.m.–6 p.m. window while this pays double, and 5-I pays double for advance sections in that same window, so overlap questions arise.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise double-time rule for a defined Sunday window on advance sections.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5-K covers the identical Sunday hours at time and one-half, so which rate applies to advance-section work is a direct clash unless 5-I is read as a carve-out.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The remedy sentence is convoluted ('the time involved in the change from the time of notice for four days'), leaving the measure of the penalty pay uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 16-M.3's no-change-in-condition rule and 20-E.7's discretion over excess holders' starting times bear on the same subject, and a supplementary agreement guarantees named holders against starting-time changes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A simple premium rule for a defined window.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It conflicts on its face with 5-I's double time for advance-section work in exactly the same Sunday hours and with 5-H's double time.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Sufficiently far ... to involve substantial travel time' is vague, and the compensation is left entirely to future negotiation — an agreement to agree.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The fallback is the Joint Standing Committee/Appeals Board under Section 16, consistent with the rest of the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Distributed unfairly' is an undefined standard, but the mandatory-overtime rule is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 8-C bars overtime discrimination against chapel chairmen and 20-C restricts Group 3/4 overtime; both are compatible.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Present practice regarding the paid lunch period shall prevail as to an outside employee' incorporates an undocumented practice, and 'sent out on paid lunch' is loosely expressed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 21-D(IV) sets a different 45-minute lunch and coffee-break regime at Newspoint expressly compensated 'as provided in Section 5N', and 22-A sets 40/30-minute lunches at Carlstadt.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Authority and control over all employees shall be vested exclusively in the office through its representative, the foreman, who shall be a member of the Union' is clear but strikingly absolute.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 6-A.2 forbids foremen from giving orders contrary to the contract and 6-B makes their terms individually negotiated, which complicates the 'exclusive' vesting; 22-A also assigns console work to journeymen 'not supervisors'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two short rules; the Union's discipline bar is qualified by 'in accordance with this agreement', which is a workable limit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 6-G gives the Publisher a complaint route if the Union imposes penalties, consistent with this.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An unrestricted appointment and removal right subject to an exception limiting foremen's performance of Section 2 work; the exception is precisely drawn.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against 4-A.1(a) placing foremen on seniority lists and 6-A.1 making the foreman a Union member, raising a coherence question about foremen's contractual status.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A narrow supervision requirement tied to two named situations; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 6-D and 3-I's right to operate either shift.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One-sentence requirement; unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits 6-A.1 and 6-C; no conflict, though 22-A's Carlstadt facility raises the question of what counts as a separate plant.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Make changes in operating procedures' is broad, and the sentence's double negative is clumsy but readable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 16-M.3 bars any change in condition without the other party's consent, which cuts against the foreman's unilateral power to change operating procedures here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Discrimination or other unfair treatment' is a general phrase after specifics, but it is a complaint route rather than a substantive duty.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 15 grievances and 16-A's thirty-day referral rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Improperly imposed penalties' is undefined, though 6-A.2 supplies the substantive rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Mirrors 6-F and is consistent with 6-A.2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Days observed as such' and the 'trips' definition (obtaining employment elsewhere in the industry on the same holiday) are workable but the forfeiture rule is narrowly drawn against a broad concept.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 7-C, 7-D and 20-D all qualify holiday entitlement, and 20-D cross-refers to 7-D and 13-B.4 in a way that is not easy to reconcile.
